result.summary: This is the surface of zig_objc, Zig bindings for the Objective-C runtime: its build.zig and build.zig.zon. The build script locates the Apple SDK via xcrun and patches one block-pointer declaration in objc/runtime.h so Zig's translate-c can handle it. It then translates the runtime headers into a module and links libobjc and Foundation; I found no network access, downloads, encoded payloads, persistence or writes outside the build cache, and the package declares no dependencies.

findings.title: Build-time patch of SDK header for translate-c
findings.detail: At build time the script reads objc/runtime.h from the Xcode SDK. It replaces the single objc_enumerateClasses declaration, whose block-pointer parameter Zig 0.16 translate-c cannot parse, with a void* parameter. It then writes the result into the build cache and translates it with the SDK headers. The patch is exact-match and fails loudly if the header changes. It only affects generated bindings and has no side effects outside the build cache.

findings.title: Runs xcrun at build time to find the SDK
findings.detail: appleSDKPath calls std.zig.system.darwin.getSdk, which runs `xcrun` to locate the Apple SDK, and caches the result per target. This is standard for building against Apple frameworks.

data_flows.what: A patched copy of the Apple SDK's objc/runtime.h and a small objc-import.h wrapper header, written at build time for translate-c.
data_flows.to: Zig build cache (WriteFiles step output directory)
